transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-23
- Time: 10:00 AM UTC
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood Solutions Eng), Michael Chen (DataNova CTO), Priya Rao (DataNova ML Eng), Samira Khan (DataNova SRE), Jordan Lee (DataNova Procurement)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync to review last week's benchmark runs comparing Redwood POC cluster vs baseline provider. Discussed p95 latency numbers, throughput (req/s), token cost delta, tuning changes (KV caching, batching, quantization profile), enterprise concerns (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and next steps for final 24h run and procurement. Shared benchmark spreadsheet and security docs links. Some transcription noise and mis-heard product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" = Dedicated).

Topics:
- Benchmark results: latency (p50/p95), throughput, error rates
- Configuration changes: KV caching, batching, quantization profile
- Tradeoffs: latency vs cost, Dedicated vs Hosted, private deployment constraints
- Security/compliance questions: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
- Next steps and procurement timeline

References shared during call:
- Benchmark spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark123
- Raw logs / Grafana dash link: https://internal.redwood/boards/datanova-poc-logs (note: internal link - actual share via email)
- Security pack (SOC2 summary, KMS integration): https://redwood.com/security/datanova-pack.pdf

Action items recap (as read out on call):
- Arjun to flip on KV caching and share config snippet + expected perf delta
- Sofia to send annotated benchmark sheet with cost calc + pricing delta
- Priya to send traffic replay file and updated success criteria
- Jordan to confirm procurement PO window and any legal timing constraints

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, rough auto transcript with occasional misrecognitions):
00:00 - Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we wanted to walk through the latest benchmark numbers from the run we did last night, should be about 30 minutes of review and then Q&A. Michael, Priya, can you confirm you see the sheet?
00:12 - Michael: Yep, I can see it. Looks like two tabs, one is the "redwood-run" and the other is "baseline-vendorx". Quick note, the baseline was run on their c5-like, we requested the same sequence lengths but I think they used a slightly different batch profile.
00:28 - Arjun: yeah, there may have been diff-ing in the batching, we tried to match but the provider used auto-batch, so take that with a grain of salt. Our configs are in the notes tab.
00:45 - Priya: ok great, on the headline numbers I'm seeing p95 latency on Redwood at ~120 ms for our 512-seq samples and baseline at ~220 ms, is that correct? There's also throughput noted as 780 req/s vs 430 req/s.
01:05 - Arjun: that's right, the 120ms p95 is with KV prefetch and 64-token micro-batching, plus our optimized kernel selection for the quantized model. Baseline numbers were without KV cache and with larger GC pauses I think. Also error rates were lower on Redwood, 0.7% vs 1.8% on their runs.
01:35 - Michael: hmm, those numbers look promising. What's the cost delta though, per million tokens? I see a line item but it's a bit unclear.
01:48 - Sofia: good question, quick answer our estimated token unit cost for this config is about $1.10 per 1M tokens compared to baseline's ~$1.45 when we factor in their less-efficient batching and higher tail latency causing re-tries — I'll send annotated calc.
02:10 - Samira: can you remind us which deployment this was on—Hosted or Dedicated? We are still leaning to dedicated pool if we move forward but we need to understand the network egress and VPC peering.
02:25 - Liam: this run was on a dedicated pilot cluster in us-east-1 with VPC peered; we used customer-managed subnet and optional private control plane. Note there are a couple of differences vs full private on-prem.
02:40 - Jordan: procurement question, if we pick Dedicated and sign a reserved commit, what's the minimum term again?
02:50 - Sofia: standard is a 3-month minimum for pilot reserved, with options to annualize; we can create a short-term pilot contract. We'll follow up with legal/terms.
03:05 - Priya: on the perf, there was mention of quantization profile, which one was used? 4-bit or 8-bit? The sheet says q4_0.
03:17 - Arjun: correct, q4_0 with some custom kernel tuning, that gave the best quality/cost balance for your workload. We also tried q8 on one run and saw marginal latency improvements but higher memory footprint. There's some transcription glitch in notes where "q for zero" was written, ignore that.
03:40 - Michael: any notable variance across time of day? Our traffic is bursty and spiky. The 24-hour run showed p95 drifting to ~150 ms during the 9am spike.
03:55 - Arjun: yes, we saw some drift during sustained burst, that's where autoscaling and burst capacity helps—our suggestion is to enable autoscale policy X with a short cooldown and prefix KV cache so warm requests hit lower latency quickly.
04:25 - Priya: can we see the KV cache hit rate numbers?
04:35 - Arjun: yep, in the grafana tab, caching hit rate averaged 78% on the representative replay for the mid-week run; that drove the big delta in per-token CPU. Baseline didn't have prefix KV in their config.
04:55 - Michael: what about consistency? If we use caching, will we risk stale info? Some of our responses require near-real-time context.
05:05 - Liam: good point, caching is prefix-based and configurable TTL; you can set TTL to a few minutes or disable for critical streams, it's flexible. We can show you config snippets.
05:28 - Jordan: security question — KMS integration, can we use our HSM? Audit logs?
05:35 - Sofia: yes, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS or partner HSMs), and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report in the follow-up.
05:50 - Samira: is the private control plane required for KMS? We prefer VPC and won't do full on-prem.
06:00 - Liam: no, VPC private control plane is enough for KMS integration, HSM on-prem only needed for air-gapped regulatory requirements.
06:18 - Priya: small nit — there's a misspelling in the sheet header, it says "KV cash" which is cute but should be "KV cache" haha.
06:25 - (laughter)
06:32 - Arjun: noted. back to perf numbers — we also ran a config with larger batching (128) and saw throughput jump to ~920 req/s but p95 increased to ~180 ms; tradeoff there. For low-latency endpoints we recommend 64 micro-batch plus prefix caching.
06:55 - Michael: and error behaviors? Retries and re-tries, any notable timeouts?
07:05 - Arjun: Timeout spikes were correlated with GC hiccups in one baseline run; on Redwood we tuned the runtime memory path and saw fewer OOM and fewer 5xx. Error rate in our run stayed under 1%.
07:25 - Priya: what's your plan to reduce p95 to below 100ms? Our bar for buying is p95 < 100ms for 90% of traffic.
07:36 - Arjun: two knobs: smaller micro-batch (32) plus more aggressive KV prefetch and a different kernel ordering; we estimate p95 ~95-100ms at cost +6-8% but we need to run a focused tuning test to confirm. Would you like us to schedule that?
07:55 - Michael: yes, run that and we'll compare to baseline under equivalent traffic.
08:05 - Sofia: noted. We'll plan a targeted tuning run next week.
08:12 - Jordan: procurement again — what do you need from our side to get pricing and contracts?
08:20 - Sofia: ideal is traffic replay + success criteria + expected query volume for next 12 months. Jordan, if you can confirm volume bands we can pull a draft SOW and pricing tiers.
08:36 - Jordan: I'll get that after this call.
08:42 - Priya: on the subject of model versions, can you pin to model sha? We don't want auto-upgrades during the POC.
08:49 - Liam: yes, you can pin model versions and we can do canary rollouts if/when you decide to upgrade.
09:02 - Michael: any compliance concerns re passing PHI? We have some redacted PII in logs.
09:10 - Sofia: Redwood supports data residency, encrypted at rest and in transit, and we can isolate logs. For PHI we recommend private deployment and additional DLP on the ingress. We'll include DLP options in the security pack.
09:30 - Arjun: quick note on the baseline run again — they used a bigger sequence distribution, which inflated their average token count; we normalized for per-token numbers but it's in the notes tab, some of the disparity is dataset difference.
09:50 - Priya: ok, so immediate ask: can you run the "aggressive low-latency" config and provide the p95 and throughput plus cost estimate?
10:00 - Arjun: yes, we'll run aggressive_lowlat config with micro-batch 32, q4_0 and aggressive KV prefetch. Expect results in 48 hours.
10:12 - Michael: great. Anything on model quality or hallucination changes with the quantization? We tested a small sample, looked similar but want more checks.
10:22 - Arjun: quantization didn't change top-k choices for your eval set in the 2k sample; we'll run a larger eval and include the eval notebook.
10:35 - Priya: one more question on network — if we peer VPC, is there any extra latency? We are sensitive to milliseconds.
10:44 - Liam: peering adds minimal ms (1-3ms) and usually preferrable vs public egress; we'll measure and include in the follow-up.
11:00 - Jordan: legal question, do you require data processing addendum?
11:08 - Sofia: yes we'll send a DPA template alongside standard MSA. We'll flag the PHI clauses.
11:20 - (brief cross talk about calendar invites and timing)
11:40 - Sofia: ok let's do a recap — action items are Arjun runs aggressive low-latency test and toggles KV cache config; Sofia will share the annotated benchmark and pricing; Priya will send traffic replay and success criteria; Jordan will confirm procurement window. We'll aim to have final 24h baseline comparison by 2026-12-27 and meet week of 2026-12-30 for final decision.
11:58 - Michael: sounds good, thanks everyone.
12:05 - Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the sheet and links.
12:15 - (call ends)
